entries.title: Sources opens on Where it sits
entries.body: If you added the article, the Sources panel opens on Where it sits: the papers that cite the article, the most important works it cites, and links to four tools. Search the literature is there too, as a button or as its report once you have run it, and no longer needs the Experimental features switch. Typing "search the literature" in the command bar opens it. Visitors to a shared article still see the Bibliography first.

entries.title: Your library shows how far you have read
entries.body: Your library shows a small pie after each article's reading time, on cards and in the table: the same mark of how far you have read as at the top of the article. It appears once you have read enough of a piece, and may be missing for some read earlier. The public library never shows it.

entries.title: Literature search looks for the piece by name
entries.body: Search the literature also looks for pages that name the piece by its title and first author. Not cited lists likely other editions, and other work by the same authors, separately. When the index of research papers holds the article twice, the papers citing it are gathered from both copies, and when the article's year is known, findings about later work leave out sources whose dates do not fit.

entries.title: Reception and Claims wait until you start them
entries.body: Opening Reception or Claims, including from the command bar, used to start their work straight away. They now wait until you press Search the web or List its claims, so nothing runs that you did not ask for.

entries.title: The top bar starts below the clock
entries.body: On the home page, Features, Pricing, Sign in, the public library and a few other pages, the bar along the top could be drawn under a phone's clock and status icons, especially in the app installed on an iPhone. It now starts below them, as it already did elsewhere.
